what_this_is: The COMPLETE list of ways the Native view is allowed to differ from the engine's Printed output. NativeVsEngineGeometryTests reads this file; any Native-vs-engine divergence it measures that is not named here FAILS. Adding a row is a deliberate act that needs a ruling behind it, not a way to quiet a red test.
why_a_file: Jon's rule is that the Printed view IS the engines' output, and that Native diverges from Printed ONLY by fonts. That is a claim about a closed set, so the set has to be written down somewhere a test can read it. Before this file the allowances lived as numeric tolerances inside individual assertions, where a new divergence of an already-tolerated shape could slip in without anyone naming it.
scope_fields: document/page/line each accept "*" for "every one". A row with document "*" is a CLASS ruling and needs its class field set; a row naming a real document, page and line is a specific accepted defect and should carry the issue that tracks it. A row may also carry `gate_reasons` and `count_ceiling`: the reason vocabulary ctrl-kd's PCL gate uses, and the most rows of those reasons this document may produce before the divergence stops being the licensed one and becomes a regression.

divergences.reason: Native sets a superscript/subscript run with Cocoa's own arithmetic - two thirds of the base font's size, with the baseline offset measured from that smaller font's own ascender/descender - where the Printed view now uses WordStar's measured per-family x-height ratio (Courier 9.25/12, banker's-rounded to a whole point size) and WordStar's own narrowed fixed-pitch cell (5.5/7.2, applied as kerning). See DocumentRenderer.scriptMetrics's `ratio` parameter and the `printedSupSub` flag threaded to it.
divergences.why_permanent: Mechanism G's ratio is measured off Courier's x-height from real WS7 PCL. Native substitutes the user's own chosen face for WordStar's, so there is no Courier x-height for that ratio to be true about - applying it there would be extrapolating a Courier measurement onto an arbitrary font. This is exactly the 'Native diverges from Printed only by fonts' rule, so it is permanent by ruling rather than pending a fix.

divergences.reason: A proportional WS5+ run lays out at the resolved Mac font's own natural advance rather than on WordStar's column grid. The engine reaches the grid with a Tz horizontal scale computed from AFM metrics; the app deliberately does not, because the Mac face it substitutes is not the face the AFM describes.
divergences.why_permanent: The MAC VIEWING RULING (decision register 2026-08-11). Job 240 removed the per-word corrective kerning that used to chase the grid - line breaks and page breaks stay engine-authoritative, which is the part that is structure; within-line placement follows the substituted font.

divergences.substituted_face: Hoefler Text (Garamond row) / Times New Roman, against the engine's base-14 Times-Bold and Times-Italic
divergences.reason: Measured through the PCL coordinate tier over the app's own Cmd-P-from-Native bytes: 1475 word-unmatched and 154 extra-word-in-engine. The document's font block is Garamond, which printedMacFontRows maps to Hoefler Text; the engine's PDF renders the same block as base-14 Times at AFM x Tz advances. Every character lands in a different place from the first proportional glyph onward, so the gate cannot pair the words at all.
divergences.why_permanent: The same MAC VIEWING RULING class as native-proportional-font-placement, observed per document rather than as a class. Recorded separately so the COUNT is pinned: a licensed divergence with no ceiling cannot tell a font substitution from a new defect hiding behind one.
divergences.ruled: 2026-08-11 (MAC VIEWING RULING), applied to this document 2026-09-07

divergences.substituted_face: Hoefler Text / Times New Roman, against the engine's base-14 Times
divergences.reason: 1057 word-unmatched and 34 extra-word-in-engine through the same tier, same cause as LYING. sr's own recorded manifest for this document is extra-word-in-engine 4 and line-start-shift 2, so the engine's PDF is nearly clean against the capture and the gap is entirely the substituted face.
divergences.ruled: 2026-08-11 (MAC VIEWING RULING), applied to this document 2026-09-07

divergences.substituted_face: the CG Times / Univers substitutes, against the engine's base-14 equivalents
divergences.reason: The heaviest proportional user in the corpus. NOTE that this document is ALSO parked for a separate reason: its capture set is v2 (Sawyer's WSCHANGE-customised install), not the v3 PRISTINE.EXE set, so it is measured against a non-pristine oracle whatever the renderer does.
divergences.why_permanent: MAC VIEWING RULING for the font half; the capture-set half is Jon's 2026-08-24 v1/v2 deprecation.
divergences.ruled: 2026-08-11 (MAC VIEWING RULING), applied to this document 2026-09-07

divergences.substituted_face: Courier Prime (1228/2048 em = 0.599609) against the engine's exact 10 CPI (0.6)
divergences.reason: Measured from the bundled font's own head/hhea/hmtx tables: Courier Prime advances 7.195312pt at 12pt where the engine's grid is exactly 7.200000pt. The shortfall is 0.004687pt per character and accumulates to at most ~0.3pt across an 80-column line. Predicts -README's observed 0.21-0.25pt residuals at columns 47-56 exactly.
divergences.why_permanent: A per-glyph corrective kern was designed and approved, then DROPPED for 4.0.3 once it was established that this surface is Native, where font metrics are licensed. It is not implemented and is recorded here rather than left as an unexplained sub-point residual. NOTE the renderer's own comment at DocumentRenderer.swift:4589 still asserts Courier 'already advances at exactly that grid' - that claim is false by 0.0047pt/char and is the reason this row exists.

divergences.reason: A run whose declared face is installed on NEITHER side is substituted TWICE, differently: the app falls through printedMacFontName to its generic primary, and the engine falls back to its own base-14 AFM metrics, which describe a different face again. The two substitutions have different advances, so the run's width differs and its ink can land in different 12pt cells. Measured 2026-09-07 on PREVIEW.WS p1's Albertus row via PixelOracleAppEngineTests: the app's line runs about 59pt wider than the engine's, producing engine-only ink at x~290 and x~363 and app-only ink at x~395-445 -- one cause appearing as BOTH missingInActual and extraInActual. Albertus is installed in none of /Library/Fonts, /System/Library/Fonts, /System/Library/Fonts/Supplemental or ~/Library/Fonts on this machine, and the app carries no explicit mapping for it.
divergences.why_permanent: The MAC VIEWING RULING (decision register 2026-08-11). This is DISTINCT from native-proportional-font-placement, which reads 'the engine reaches the grid with a Tz horizontal scale computed from AFM metrics' -- that row assumes the engine HAS the face's own metrics and only the app substitutes. When the face is absent from base-14 too, neither side has them and the divergence is between two substitutions rather than between a substitution and the truth. Naming it separately keeps that distinction visible; folding it into the other row would assert an AFM the engine does not have.
